verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California, at 8:07 p.m. EDT on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) ... Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'splash down at about 8:07 p.m. ET Friday, April 10, 2026, off the coast of San Diego, California'; R1: 'splashdown in the Pacific on Friday ... off the San Diego coast'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm location, time, date, and successful splashdown in Pacific near San Diego.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Textbook touchdown for Artemis II astronauts'; R5: '"textbook touchdown"'; R6: '"textbook touchdown"'
verifications.reasoning: Exact phrase used in multiple sources to describe the splashdown.

verifications.claim: The splashdown marked the end of a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'approximate 10-day mission'; R4: '10-day journey'; R5: '10-day moon voyage'; R6: '10-day journey'; R1: 'nearly 10-day flight'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe the mission duration as 10 days or nearly 10 days, rounded to 10.

verifications.claim: The mission had a crew of four.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'crew of four'; R2: 'four astronauts'; R4: 'four astronauts'; R5: 'four-member crew'; R6: 'four-person crew'
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state crew of four.

verifications.claim: The crew of four was in good health.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'happy and healthy'; R6: 'happy and healthy'; R2: 'safely aboard ... post-mission medical evaluations'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly report crew as happy, healthy, and safe post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule was successfully retrieved by Navy teams.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'U.S. Navy helicopters ... Navy divers ... USS John P. Murtha'; R5: 'Navy helicopters ... US Navy USS John P. Murtha'; R6: 'US helicopters ... USS John P Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm successful retrieval by U.S. Navy teams and vessel.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule hit the water at approximately 20 mph.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'slowing to a 19 mp/h (30 km/h) splashdown'; R4: 'slow Orion ... to just 17 mph before the spacecraft lands'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state 17-19 mph at splashdown, directly supporting 'approximately 20 mph'.

verifications.claim: Five orange airbags activated to flip the Artemis II Orion capsule upright.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'five orange airbags will inflate around the top of the spacecraft and flip the capsule into an upright position'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is the first crewed, deep-space journey of the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first lunar voyage in more than a half-century ... NASA’s long-awaited lunar comeback'; R6: 'first people to travel to the Moon in more than half a century'; R5: 'first crewed mission to the moon since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm as first crewed lunar/deep-space mission in Artemis program (post uncrewed Artemis I).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is designed to test equipment for future lunar surface landings.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first major step in establishing a sustainable moon base ... Artemis IV will attempt to land'; R6: 'sets the stage for future lunar landings'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe Artemis II as foundational step enabling future landings, but not explicitly testing surface landing equipment (focus on Orion/SLS for deep space).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is set to be extracted from the Artemis II Orion capsule by Amentum recovery teams.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Amentum recovery team ... safely retrieving the Artemis II crew'
verifications.reasoning: Source directly names Amentum teams for crew extraction.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is set to return to the Navy vessel
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'flown to the USS John P. Murtha'; R5: 'airlifting them to the US Navy USS John P. Murtha'; R6: 'hoisted into US helicopters and flown to the USS John P Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm crew transport to Navy vessel USS John P. Murtha.
